title: Resolving the extended stellar atmospheres of asymptotic giant branch stars at (sub)millimetre wavelengths
question: What are the brightness temperature structure, hotspots, variability and opacity structure of the extended atmospheres of four nearby AGB stars at (sub)mm wavelengths?

what.value: Stellar radii R_* adopted from near-IR measurements (Mira A, R Leo) and others

evidence.quote: We used $R_*=15$ mas, which is the smallest measurement of (cite: Woodruff2009) in the analysis.

what.value: Absorption coefficients for electron-neutral free-free opacity (third-order polynomial fits)

evidence.quote: To calculate the opacity, we use the RM97 third-order polynomial fits to the absorption coefficients calculated by (cite: DL66).

what.value: Mira B subtracted from Mira A data

evidence.quote: For Mira A, we performed the fits after its companion Mira B was subtracted from the data.

recipe.method: Inspect calibration, extra flagging, recalibrate R Leo Band 4 fluxes, phase-only self-calibration

recipe.goal: Fit uniform elliptical disc in uv plane per spw
recipe.method: Fit flux density, major axis, axis ratio and position angle per spw
key_parameters: uv range restricted to >2 Mlambda (Band 4) or >3 Mlambda (Bands 6,7) for spws with short-baseline excess

recipe.goal: Derive brightness temperature and spectral index
recipe.method: T_b from flux, size, axis ratio, frequency; spectral index via Monte Carlo with flux uncertainties
assumptions: 10% absolute flux uncertainty per band (5% for R Leo Band 4)

recipe.method: Power-law density and grey/power-law temperature, ionisation power law, electron-neutral free-free opacity, Rayleigh-Jeans radiative transfer; compare size-frequency and T_b-size relations; add layer with 10x tau_ff increase at R_s
assumptions: Only atomic hydrogen interacts with electrons (no molecular H2 equilibrium)

recipe.method: Scale sizes to common frequencies and fit linear size growth over time

answer_key.quantity: R Leo expansion velocity of mm surface

evidence.quote: for R Leo we directly measure an outward motion of the millimetre wavelength surface with a velocity of at least $10.6\pm1.4$ km s$^{-1}$
We can fit a linear expansion of $0.17\pm0.02$ mas day$^{-1}$ to the Band 4 data
$\eta=-0.087\pm0.006$ is determined from the Band 4 and 6 observations

answer_key.quantity: R Dor hotspot brightness above disc (Band 7)

evidence.quote: we can determine a lower limit to $T_{\rm b}$ for both brightest hotspot of $>3300$ K above the average stellar disc temperature
In Band 7, the two spots are very compact ($<2.6\times2.6$ mas) with $T_{\rm b}>10000$ K.
requires a sudden increase (moving inwards) in opacity by at least a factor of 10 at $R_s=1.4~R_*$

not_stated_but_needed: uvmultifit settings (initial guesses, weights, per-spw handling)
line-free channel selection and self-cal solution intervals
image sizes, cell sizes and clean parameters
model fitting procedure for atmosphere parameters (done by eye or fit?)
uv-range cutoffs per spw for all sources
score_reason: Public data and clear uv-fit approach, but calibration details and model-tuning procedure are loosely specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, uv-disc fits give numeric sizes, fluxes and T_b in Table 2 that can be re-derived, though the model step is less specified.
